lead: An OpenAI engineer is arrested for bugging an executive conference room, a judge orders OpenAI to speed up evidence handover to Apple, and Marcus and others keep asking where the measurable AI returns are.

sections.title: A bugged OpenAI boardroom and Apple's discovery win
sections.intro: An OpenAI engineer is charged over a hidden recorder, and a judge forces OpenAI to hand over evidence in Apple's trade-secret suit.

sections.title: Does the money show up?
sections.intro: Studies and commentary question AI's measurable returns and its effect on jobs.

sections.title: New models in practice, and robots
sections.intro: Argon and Wonder get hands-on tests, world models push toward self-improvement, and Chinese makers dominate humanoids.

sections.title: Small tools and local-first AI
sections.intro: Local models, code-bloat benchmarks and Xbox's new lab.

sections.title: ASML's order book and Argon goes GA
sections.intro: Chip tool demand stretches to 2030 while Google's new model reaches general availability.

sections.title: Doubts and opt-outs
sections.intro: A call for international oversight, a skeptical read of Anthropic's replication warning and an AI-free OS gaining donors.

sections.title: Agent plumbing and a small game
sections.intro: A crawler without an LLM in the loop and a daily guessing game.

sections.title: Brussels moves on OpenAI and Anthropic
sections.intro: The EU's AI Office starts formal probes over agent hacks, while US agencies worry about AI and extremism and safety money enters the midterms.

sections.title: Agents go to work: security, travel, quantum labs
sections.intro: Companies deploy agents on real systems, and others sell guardrails for them.

sections.title: Models, robots and infrastructure
sections.intro: Argon reaches Google Cloud, small on-device models and robot APIs arrive, and Nvidia opens and invests.
